key_insight: A control- and game-theory grounded computational framework models co-adaptation between human users and decoders in closed-loop neural interfaces, enabling principled prediction and shaping of interaction dynamics to improve usability and personalization.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of formal, predictive models for how users and adaptive decoders jointly evolve in closed-loop neural interfaces, which has prevented principled design of decoders that steer learning and performance.
method: Formulate the user–decoder interaction as a coupled control/game-theoretic system to capture bidirectional adaptation and learning dynamics.
Analyze equilibria and transient dynamics to derive design principles for closed-loop decoders that shape user behavior and improve co-adaptation outcomes.
Validate the framework via theoretical analysis and computational experiments to demonstrate how decoder design choices affect usability and personalization.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a rigorous toolkit to predict and engineer co-adaptive human–machine systems, enabling more reliable, personalized, and efficient neural interfaces and informing design choices for closed-loop adaptive algorithms.
visual_elements: Schematic loop diagram showing bidirectional adaptation: user ↔ decoder with feedback arrows and objective functions for each agent
Phase portrait or trajectory plots illustrating co-adaptation dynamics and convergence to equilibria under different decoder designs
Flowchart summarizing design rules: inputs (metrics & objectives) → analysis (game/control) → decoder update policy → predicted user outcome
Before/after usability bar chart or performance curves comparing standard vs. framework-guided decoder designs
paper_title: Computational framework to predict and shape human–machine interactions in closed-loop, co-adaptive neural interfaces
paper_authors: Maneeshika M. Madduri, Momona Yamagami, Si Jia Li, Sasha Burckhardt, Samuel A. Burden
